 State shares provisional ballot numbers for ENC 
 Duplin County Polling Early Voting (WITN) By WITN Web Team Published : Nov. 5, 2026 at 1:33 PM EST | Updated : 2 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google The above video is our WITN+ livestream and may not reflect the content in this story. 
 RALEIGH, N.C. (WITN) - The State Board of Elections has released the number of provisional ballots cast during early voting and on Election Day during the 2026 midterms.
 Across North Carolina, state election officials say 36,737 provisional ballots were cast during the 2026 General Election. In eastern Carolina, there were 3,101 voters used provisional ballots, with 2,678 of those being cast on Election Day.
 Pitt County had the most provision ballots cast in the east, with 1,116. Second was Onslow County with 455 and third was Craven County with 285.
 Statewide, Wake County cast the most provisional ballots, with 3,337. Mecklenburg County is second with 3,142 provisional ballots.
 A voter can cast a provisional ballot when their name does not appear on the voter registration rolls for the voting location or other questions arise about eligibility to vote. If they show up without an acceptable photo ID, a voter can also submit a provisional ballot and either complete a Photo ID Exception Form at the voting site or go to their county elections board with the approved ID by noon on the fifth business day since Election Day.
 Each county board will meet and decide to approve, partially approve or disapprove of each provisional ballot after Election Day. If deemed eligible, the ballot is counted.
 The provisional ballot votes will get added to results during the 10-day canvass period, the state elections board says. County canvass is set for next Friday, while State canvass will be held on November 24.
 The state says its chart will be updated as additional counties report provisional ballot numbers to the board.
